title: Free-living physical-behaviour metrics on real accelerometry, with ENMO validated against GGIR to machine precision

dataset.name: PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring
dataset.record: subject101 (Protocol), hand IMU +/-16g tri-axial acceleration @ 100 Hz; ~1 h of gap-free samples from a scripted activity protocol (lie/sit/stand/walk/run/cycle/iron/vacuum)
dataset.citation: Reiss A, Stricker D. Introducing a New Benchmarked Dataset for Activity Monitoring. IEEE ISWC 2012, pp. 108-109; dataset doi:10.24432/C5NW2H (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: Free-living physical-behaviour analysis rests on one metric -- ENMO, the Euclidean-norm-minus-one acceleration. On real continuous accelerometer data the ecosystem's computeENMO() reproduces the field-standard GGIR implementation to MACHINE PRECISION (max absolute difference 1.35e-14 g, correlation 1.000000 across 749 five-second epochs). On that exact foundation the free-living summary runs end to end -- intensity time-use, the Rowlands intensity gradient (-1.19) and activity fragmentation (active-to-sedentary transition probability 0.11) -- turning a raw recording into the ICF performance picture of what a person actually does.

claims.statement: max absolute ENMO difference vs GGIR (g) -- machine precision
ENMO correlation vs GGIR across 749 epochs
Rowlands intensity gradient (log-log slope of time vs intensity)

validation.reference: GGIR (van Hees et al.) -- the field-standard free-living accelerometry package; computeENMO is checked against GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMO on the identical raw signal
validation.data: REAL -- PAMAP2 subject101 hand IMU (Reiss & Stricker 2012), ~1 h continuous @ 100 Hz
validation.note: The RIGOROUS, transferable result is the ENMO reproduction: two independent implementations agree to 1e-14 g on real data, so the physical-activity foundation is exact. The summary metrics (intensity gradient, MVPA, fragmentation) are DEMONSTRATED on a real continuous recording, but PAMAP2 is a scripted activity PROTOCOL, not a free-living day -- the absolute values reflect the protocol, and the ~1 h length makes the MX metrics (e.g. M60) degenerate, so those are not claimed. The pipeline and the ENMO exactness transfer; a specific person's free-living numbers do not.

open_questions.q: PAMAP2 is a lab protocol, so the intensity time-use is not a real-world day; validating the full free-living summary needs a genuinely free-living public recording (e.g. a wrist dataset with a worn day). Documented, not escalated.
